text:
Predicates:
Contains(x, y) ::: x contains y.
Read(x, y) ::: x reads y.
Gains(x, y) ::: x gains y.
Smarter(x) ::: x is smarter.
Premises:
∀x (Book(x) → ∃y (Contains(x, y) ∧ Knowledge(y))) ::: Books contain tons of knowledge.
∀x ∀y (Read(x, y) ∧ Book(y) → Gains(x, Knowledge)) ::: When a person reads a book, that person gains knowledge.
∀x (Gains(x, Knowledge) → Smarter(x)) ::: If a person gains knowledge, they become smarter.
Read(harry, walden) ::: Harry read the book 'Walden' by Henry Thoreau.
Conclusion:
∀x (Smarter(x) → Gains(x, Knowledge)) ::: A smarter person has gained knowledge.
